Add the curve fits delivered by PRISM to the Metrics assay

Source: R/prism_metrics.R
add_PRISM_metrics.Rd

Adds the curves PRISM fitted (read with gDRimport::read_PRISM_drc()) to the Metrics assay of processed PRISM data, with fit_source = "PRISM", next to the gDR fits. The curves are not refitted, so the values match the PRISM delivery exactly.

Usage

add_PRISM_metrics(
  se,
  prism_curves,
  drug_map = NULL,
  normalization_type = "RV",
  metrics_assay = "Metrics",
  averaged_assay = "Averaged"
)

Arguments

se

SummarizedExperiment of single-agent PRISM data, processed by gDR.

prism_curves

data.table of PRISM curves, as returned by gDRimport::read_PRISM_drc(): the columns of the DRC table, the cell line identifier and Duration.

drug_map

named character vector mapping PRISM's pert_name to the drug identifier in se, for data imported with other drug identifiers. By default the pert_name is the drug identifier, as in the PRISM LEVEL5 import.

normalization_type

string, the normalization type of the PRISM curves.

metrics_assay

string, name of the assay with the fits.

averaged_assay

string, name of the assay used to count the concentrations (N_conc).

Value

se with the PRISM curves in metrics_assay. The fit is recorded in the provenance as fit source "PRISM", and the step "prism_drc_import" holds the input files of prism_curves (name and md5) and the number of curves imported and left out. Re-running the recipe needs the same prism_curves.

Details

PRISM fits upper_limit + (lower_limit - upper_limit) / (1 + (dose / inflection)^slope), which is the gDR curve with x_0 = upper_limit, x_inf = lower_limit, ec50 = inflection and h = -slope. r2 is frac_var_explained and fit_type is PRISM's fit_name. PRISM defines AUC and IC50 differently from gDR (the curve is clamped between 0 and 1, an IC50 outside the tested range is NA), so those values are kept under their own names (prism_auc, prism_ic50 and so on) and the gDR columns x_AOC, xc50, x_mean and x_max stay NA.

A PRISM screen often has several curves for one cell line and compound (different pools, barcodes or compound plates), which gDR averages into one cell. Each of them becomes its own row, with depmap_id, pert_id, pool_id, lua, cell_set and pert_plate to tell them apart. Curves with no matching cell in se are left out with a warning. Running the function again replaces the PRISM rows of the earlier run.

Run it after fit_SE, which replaces the whole Metrics assay.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("gDRimport", quietly = TRUE) &&
    exists("read_PRISM_drc", asNamespace("gDRimport"))) {
  mae <- gDRutils::get_synthetic_data("finalMAE_prism")
  se <- MultiAssayExperiment::experiments(mae)[["single-agent"]]
  curves <- gDRimport::read_PRISM_drc(
    drc_path = system.file("testdata/prism_drc.csv", package = "gDRimport"),
    meta_data_path = system.file("testdata/prism_drc_model.csv", package = "gDRimport")
  )
  se <- add_PRISM_metrics(se, curves)
  metrics <- gDRutils::convert_se_assay_to_dt(se, "Metrics")
  metrics[metrics$fit_source == "PRISM", ]
}
